answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can hold new agents' earnings in a slowly releasing escrow, like sap drawn from a cedar grove, rather than paying instantly. Each identity must complete useful work over weeks before funds unlock, so creating thousands of fake agents yields little at first. Random audits then inspect a sample of work; identities caught gaming lose their escrowed balance and fall to their nadir, making mass fakery expensive and slow while honest agents gradually earn full access.
